module.name: pinstore
module.spec: FileStateStore.Load reads .drift/state.xml via the caller-provided fileio.Session (see fileio.session), unmarshals XML into Specs, Markers, and Edges, and returns the State. State.xml version=4 is the provenance-closure format: baseline only, no <edgeResolutions>. Pre-v4 files are refused with ErrStateVersionUnsupported, directing the user to delete .drift/ and re-init. If the file does not exist, it returns ErrStateNotFound.

FileStateStore.Save marshals State to indented XML and writes it to .drift/state.xml via the caller-provided fileio.Session (see fileio.write_atomicity), which atomically replaces any existing file via temp-file + rename. The XML root element is drift (version 4) with nested specs, markers, and edges sections. Before marshalling, Save validates the referential-closure invariant via validateEdgeEndpoints: every edge endpoint (From and To) must resolve to a node (spec or marker) in the same State, since marker→spec and spec→spec edges are both legitimate; a violation returns ErrDanglingEdge without writing. This makes dangling-edge corruption unreachable from any writer, not just the current call sites. Save does not create directories or take locks; the Session owns both concerns.
When .drift/state.xml does not exist on disk, Load returns ErrStateNotFound, prompting the user to run drift init first.

State{Specs, Markers, Edges} is the in-memory shape of .drift/state.xml — a snapshot of every tracked node and edge. Specs and Markers carry their baseline hash (an empty hash means "newly reconciled, not yet baselined"); Edges is the unified list of link-style (marker→spec) and ref-style (spec→spec) edges. The StateStore interface declares three methods: Load(sess) reads state.xml via the caller-provided Session; Save(sess, state) writes it; Initialized() (no Session — runs outside any transaction) reports whether state.xml exists on disk. FileStateStore is the production implementation, constructed via NewFileStateStore(dir) where dir is the project root (the store joins dir with ".drift/state.xml" internally). Dir() returns the stored directory. See pinstore.load, pinstore.save, pinstore.initialized.

Initialized() reports whether .drift/state.xml exists on disk by calling os.Stat on the joined path. It returns (true, nil) when the file exists, (false, nil) when os.IsNotExist matches, and (false, err) for any other stat error (e.g. permission denied). Critically, Initialized does NOT take a Session — it runs outside any transaction because its primary caller, the orchestrator's Init method, uses it to decide whether to attempt a Save at all (and only then begin a write transaction). This means a concurrent Init from another process could create state.xml between the Initialized check and the subsequent Save, but the Save path is idempotent (it just overwrites with empty state) — the cli.init_idempotent layer catches the "already initialized" case via StateStore.Save semantics. See cli.init_idempotent, orch.orchestrator_construction.

stateFileXML is the encoding/xml decoder shape for state.xml. The root element is <drift version="4">; the version attribute is omitted when zero (only on the legacy pre-v4 files that Load refuses). Specs serialize under <specs><spec id hash filepath line>...</specs>; Markers under <markers><marker id hash filepath line endline>...</markers>; Edges under <edges><edge from to>...</edges>. specXML carries four attributes; markerXML carries five (adding endline for the range-end line number). edgeXML is just {From, To}. The const stateFileName = "state.xml" centralizes the filename. version=4 is the provenance-closure format (baseline only, no <edgeResolutions>); pre-v4 files are refused on Load with ErrStateVersionUnsupported directing the user to delete .drift/ and re-init. See pinstore.load, pinstore.save, pinstore.state_shape.

validateEdgeEndpoints(state) enforces the persistence-boundary invariant that every edge endpoint (From and To) in a State resolves to a node (spec or marker) in that same State. The check builds a union set of spec IDs and marker IDs, then walks every edge and returns ErrDanglingEdge (wrapping "from=X to=Y") on the first endpoint that doesn't resolve. The check runs inside Save BEFORE marshalling, so no writer can persist a state with a dangling edge — neither a typo in a freshly-added ref nor an edge left behind by a NODE_REMOVED reset. Marker→spec and spec→spec edges are both legitimate, so endpoints are resolved against the union (not against specs or markers separately). This invariant previously held only implicitly and was violated by reset accepting a spec deletion while a citer's edge still pointed at the removed spec; enforcing it at the persistence boundary makes the class of bug unreachable from any writer, not just the current call sites. See pinstore.save.

BaselineStore manages content-addressed baseline content packed in a single .drift/baselines.bin file, gob-encoded as a map[string]string (hash → content). For markers, the hash is sha1(content). For specs, the hash is the canonical hash (sha1 of spec content with <ref> tags stripped, see scanner.spec_discovery); the stored content is the raw innerxml including refs so that drift diff and drift show display faithful spec text. The legacy sha1(content)==hash integrity check is therefore not enforced — drift's own scanner produces matching pairs, and the display concern outweighs the integrity net for spec baselines. Read(sess, hash) loads the packfile via Session.Read, unmarshals, and returns content for hash or false if missing. Write(sess, hash, content) loads the packfile, updates the map, marshals, and atomic-writes via Session.Write (see fileio.write_atomicity). Delete(sess, hash) removes the entry and persists. All three operations route through the caller-provided fileio.Session; the Session's lock serializes concurrent writers. See principles.specs_are_truth — content-addressed by canonical hash, and see fileio.session.
